summary.name: NVIDIA NGC
summary.one_liner: NVIDIA NGC is NVIDIA's portal for GPU-optimized AI and HPC software, including containers, pretrained models, Jupyter notebooks, Helm charts, enterprise services and support.
use_cases: Deploying GPU-optimized AI frameworks in containers
Finding pretrained models for computer vision or speech AI
Sharing proprietary AI containers and models within an enterprise
Running AI workloads on Kubernetes or edge systems
Trying generative AI models in a browser before integrating via API
summary.what_it_does: NGC is a catalog of GPU-accelerated containers for frameworks such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, MXNet, TensorRT and RAPIDS, tested to run on supported NVIDIA GPUs. It also hosts pretrained models with model cards, Jupyter notebook tutorials, Helm charts, and industry SDKs. A Private Registry lets enterprises store and share custom containers and models securely. NVIDIA AI Foundation models can be tried in a browser, called through APIs, or run on Windows machines with RTX GPUs. The page says software runs on bare metal, Kubernetes, virtual machines, on-prem, cloud and edge, and it links to NVIDIA AI Enterprise for enterprise support.
notable: Containers are scanned monthly for security, with reports provided
Pretrained model cards describe architecture, training data and limitations
Private Registry for sharing proprietary containers and models within an enterprise
Available through major cloud provider VM marketplaces and Kubernetes services
caveats: Running NGC software in the cloud incurs each cloud provider's GPU instance pricing
Full enterprise support and long-term support require NVIDIA AI Enterprise licenses
Software is aimed at NVIDIA GPU hardware; supported NVIDIA GPUs are required
